subject.title: feat(agents): rename scheduler agent tool cron -> automations

question: Should the migration preserve legacy `cron` only at external invocation boundaries for a defined transition window while Doctor rewrites persisted tool-policy values to `automations` before runtime evaluation?
rationale: The repository policy forbids normal-runtime compatibility readers for retired config shapes, while preserving old MCP and Gateway callers is a separate public-contract decision that needs an explicit owner-approved lifetime.

options.title: Doctor-migrate config; retain bounded call aliases
options.body: Rewrite persisted policy values through Doctor and preserve legacy MCP/Gateway invocation aliases only under a documented transition and removal plan.

options.title: Canonical-only cutover
options.body: Remove legacy invocation aliases as well and require clients to use `automations`, accepting a breaking external-tool rename.

options.title: Approve permanent aliases
options.body: Explicitly adopt permanent `cron` compatibility across configuration and external invocation despite the runtime-canonicalization policy.

recommendation.title: Doctor-migrate config; retain bounded call aliases
recommendation.body: Rewrite persisted policy values through Doctor and preserve legacy MCP/Gateway invocation aliases only under a documented transition and removal plan.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor authored the RFC-linked identity and compatibility design, so they are the best available routing contact for documenting its intended boundary; final acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
